nm north of Empire Mica Wreck to 66 nm southwest of C Tower, moving

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is ongoing.

* WHERE...Northern Liberty County in southeastern Texas...
Southeastern Polk County in southeastern Texas...
East Central San Jacinto County in southeastern Texas...

* WHEN...Until 1015 AM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Numerous roads
remain closed due to flooding including FM 943 at Menard Creek near
Segno.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 743 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Flooding is already occurring in the warned area.
Between 6 and 16 inches of rain have fallen.
- Rainfall is beginning to filter back into Polk County. Additional
rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are possible in the warned
area. If rainfall persists for an extended period of time or if
rain rates increase, this may need to be upgraded to a Flash
Flood Warning again.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Shepherd, Goodrich, Alabama-Coushatta Reservation and Segno.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 3 at 8:23AM CDT until September 3 at 8:45AM CDT by NWS Milwaukee/Sullivan WI
properties.description:
At 822 AM CDT, a severe thunderstorm was located over River Hills, or
over Glendale, moving east at 35 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and penny size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

Locations impacted include...
Northern Milwaukee, Menomonee Falls, Mequon, Whitefish Bay, Brown
Deer, Fox Point, Bayside, Thiensville, Glendale, River Hills, and
Shorewood.

People attending Glendale Nights on the Patio  should seek safe
shelter immediately!
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

NWSheadline: A SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 845 AM CDT FOR SOUTHWESTERN OZAUKEE AND NORTHERN MILWAUKEE COUNTIES

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 3 at 9:14AM EDT until September 3 at 9:45AM EDT by NWS State College PA
properties.description:
At 914 AM EDT, a severe thunderstorm was located near Buffalo Mills,
or 5 miles west of Bedford, moving southeast at 55 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

Locations impacted include...
Bedford, Clearville, Everett, Buffalo Mills, Cessna, Schellsburg,
Manns Choice, New Paris and Rainsburg.

This includes the following highways...
The Pennsylvania Turnpike between mile markers 130 and 159.
Interstate 99 between mile markers 0 and 6.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds and large
hail.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 3 at 8:09AM EDT until September 3 at 6:00PM EDT by NWS Mount Holly NJ
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Mount Holly has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in Pennsylvania...

East Branch Brandywine Creek Below Downingtown affecting Chester
County.

For the Brandywine Creek...including Downingtown...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...East Branch Brandywine Creek below Downingtown.

* WHEN...From this morning to this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, Dowlin Forge Road begins to flood.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:45 AM EDT Thursday the stage was 7.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:45 AM EDT Thursday was 7.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage late
this morning and continue falling to 3.5 feet tomorrow afternoon.
- Flood stage is 7.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 7.2
feet on 03/01/2021.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/phi.

The next statement will be issued this evening by 600 PM EDT.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 3 at 7:22AM CDT until September 3 at 10:30AM CDT by NWS Bismarck ND
properties.description:
FFWBIS

The National Weather Service in Bismarck has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central McHenry County in north central North Dakota...

* Until 1030 AM CDT.

* At 722 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 4 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Towner, Granville, Denbigh, and Simcoe.
